Adverse reaction to medication kills many fish at Texas State Aquarium

As a long time member of the Texas State Aquarium, this news is a horrible tragedy to me personally. My family and I have seen these affected exhibits so many times that I feel like I lost many friends to a senseless accident. The Islands of Steel exhibit was always our main attraction as it had the most diverse and interesting fish and other marine life. The green moray eel I loved to see appears to have been one of the casualties. I hope the lab test results don't make this story worse by showing the cause to be a manufacturing error or product negligence that could have been avoided with better testing or quality control. Having known several of the Marine Biologists who have cared for the marine life there over the years, I know they are reeling from the loss. I can only imagine the panic and desperate agony they must have felt as each of these gentle creatures succumbed to the life robbing reaction. I don't know how the aquarium will recover from this tragic disaster. I can only hope there will be an outpouring of help, kindness and community charity to help our beloved aquarium pull through these tough times.

For my fish friends, I will miss you and remember you in the pictures you gave me and my family. It saddens me to lose you all.
